events.reasoning: The program runs and produces the expected three-column table for the given example (and most typical URLs), but it does not fully implement the specification: 1. Final URL on error is wrong after redirects. The spec says: if the final response status is not 2xx, use `(error)` for the title and the ORIGINAL URL for the final URL. The code first calls `get_final_url()` (which returns `response.url`, i.e. the post-redirect URL, even for 4xx/5xx), then issues a second request and, in the `else` branch, only sets `title = '(error)'` without resetting `final_url = url`. So for a URL that redirects to a non-2xx page (e.g. `https://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=https://httpbin.org/status/404`), the report shows the redirected URL instead of the original URL. It only happens to be correct when there is no redirect, because then `response.url == url`. 2. Not decoded as UTF-8. The spec explicitly requires decoding the body as UTF-8; the code uses `response.text`, which honors the Content-Type charset (or chardet `apparent_encoding`) instead, so titles can differ from the required UTF-8 decoding. 3. Title extraction differs from the spec. The spec defines the title as the raw text between the first `` and the first following `` (case-insensitive). The code instead uses BeautifulSoup, whose HTML parsing can produce different results for malformed markup (e.g. a `` with no closing tag yields text instead of `(no title)`). 4. Cells are written unescaped, so a title/final URL containing `<` or `</td>` can break the table rather than "contain the corresponding text." The double request per URL and the unused `time` import are not functional problems by themselves, but the first request/second request split is what introduces bug #1. For the provided example the output is correct, but the code does not meet the spec's error-handling and decoding requirements in general.

Link Report

""" for url, title, final_url in data: html += f""" """ html += """

{url} {title} {final_url}

events.reasoning: The code builds the required HTML table and follows redirects, but it does not correctly implement several required behaviors. Most importantly, it never checks the final HTTP status code. `requests.get()` does not raise an exception for 4xx/5xx responses, so URLs returning 404/500/etc. will still be parsed for a title and will keep their redirected/final URL instead of setting the title to `(error)` and the final URL to the original URL. It also makes two separate requests per URL, so the final URL and title/error state can come from different requests, which can violate the required paired error behavior. Additionally, it uses `response.text`, which uses headers/guessed encoding, not explicitly UTF-8 decoding as required. Finally, using BeautifulSoup's `get_text(strip=True)` is not exactly the required extraction of raw text between the first `<title>` and first `</title>`; it strips whitespace, decodes entities, and returns an empty string for an empty `<title>` rather than `(no title)`.
